citation.note: Earned Paid Leave (26 M.R.S. § 637): 40-hour minimum EPL for 10+ employees (1 hour per 40 hours worked); all accrued, unused EPL must be paid out at termination.

body.interaction_rule: Earned Paid Leave (26 M.R.S. § 637): 40-hour minimum EPL for 10+ employees (1 hour per 40 hours worked); all accrued, unused EPL must be paid out at termination. Paid Family and Medical Leave (26 M.R.S. § 850-A et seq.): 12-week paid leave, benefits from 2026-05-01.

Pay frequency and final pay (26 M.R.S. § 621-A, § 626): Wages paid at least weekly; final paycheck due on next regular payday.

body.deadline_description: Final paycheck due on next regular payday unless employee resigns without notice or is discharged (verify timing for discharge final pay) (26 M.R.S. § 621-A).

citation.note: Non-compete restrictions (26 M.R.S. § 599-A, § 599-B): Non-competes enforceable only if employee earns at least 400% of federal poverty level (approximately $62,920 annually); 3-business-day pre-signing notice; 1-2 year term cap.

body.rule: Non-compete restrictions (26 M.R.S. § 599-A, § 599-B): Non-competes enforceable only if employee earns at least 400% of federal poverty level (approximately $62,920 annually); 3-day pre-signing notice (3 business days before signing); 1-2 year term cap.

citation.note: Severance for plant closings (26 M.R.S. § 635): Employers with 100+ employees at a worksite must provide 90 days' notice and severance equal to 1 week's pay per year of service (up to 26 weeks).

Pay statement requirements (26 M.R.S. § 631): Itemized statements showing gross wages, deductions, and net wages; electronic or paper delivery with employee consent.
Contractor classification (26 M.R.S. § 602): Maine applies the economic realities test to determine contractor vs. employee status for wage-and-hour law and workers' compensation.

citation.note: Employee access to personnel files (26 M.R.S. § 631): Employee may obtain copies within 10 days of request; employer may charge a reasonable copying fee (not to exceed actual cost of reproduction).
Pay transparency protection: Employees have right to discuss wages with coworkers without retaliation (implied under § 626-B public policy exception).
Substance use testing (26 M.R.S. § 683): Maine law does not mandate drug testing but permits pre-employment, reasonable-suspicion, and post-accident testing with written policy notice.
Breach notification (10 M.R.S. § 1348): 30-day notice with AG notice at 100+ residents.
